newsitem.title: UK: Santos features as origin in sugar freight enquiry.
newsitem.headline: Santos features as origin in sugar freight enquiry.

text.p: South Brazil's key port of Santos started to feature gradually as a quoted origin on London's sugar freight market as it gears up for its 1997 programme of shipments, market sources said on Tuesday.
Cargill returned to the market with another south Brazil order, quoting for a prompt 25,000 tonnes min/max, again in bulk, from Paranagua or Santos to Black sea, Baltic or Egyptian Mediterranean.
Genoc was open for 5/7,000 tonnes, reported to be mixed but mostly bagged sugar, from Santos to west Africa for prompt shipment.
Union officials in Brazil said chances were slim for a stevedores strike at the port thanks to progress made in talks between union representatives and local steel firm Cosipa.
Union members staged two strikes at Santos in April in protest against a Cosipa decision to use its own workers to load and unload vessels at its private terminal.
Other new orders included one from CSR, which quoted for 20,000 tonnes min/max bulk sugar from its usual Queensland origin to Surabaya for June 1/10.
Tate & Lyle entered the market with an enquiry for 12,200 tonnes of bulk sugar from Belize to London or Greenock for June 8/15.
Of the day's firmer business, shipbrokers said E D & F Man fixed 25,000 tonnes from the Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic. No rate has yet been reported.
Man was also said to be working, or possibly already fixed, 13/15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Algeria for the end of May.
Jean Lion fixed 13/13,500 tonnes in bulk from Thailand to south China, although shipbrokers said they were unclear about the fixture's shipment dates.
